content:
alexa: FYI we're seeing a new cluster of fncall validation failures after the strict schema gate went live on canary routes. Console is filled with 'reject' badges and a few customers pinged SE.

tom: what kind of rejects? parse errors or shape mismatches?

alexa: mostly shape mismatches. example: tool 'user_lookup' returned an array where schema expects object. some are also enums with new values from customer tool adapters.

ridhi: example log: ```json
{
  \"route_id\": \"orders-readonly\",
  \"tool\": \"user_lookup\",
  \"result\": \"declined\",
  \"reason\": \"type_mismatch:expected_object_got_array\",
  \"raw_sample\": \"[[\\\"id\\\":\"u-1\"]]\"\n}
```

observability-bot: metric alert created: validation.declines.rate > 0.75% for route orders-readonly (last 5m).

tom: product/UX question: should console show the raw_sample inline? devs want it to debug quickly but legal wants default redaction.

alexa: ops proposal: show a single-line redacted snippet and a button 'Request full trace' that creates a ticket with audit logging. Allow customers to opt-in to store full samples per route.

ridhi: we need clear billing rules too. Right now declined fncalls still count toward token usage because model responded. Billing-bot: notify finance thread.

billing-bot: note: existing invoices include declined token consumption. Please confirm new policy before changing billing behavior.

tom: my stance: bill only when the validation outcome is 'accepted' or when a permissive fallback accepted the tool (attribution to the accepting route). If strict gate declines and fallback wasn't used, mark non-billable.

alexa: edge-case: retries & async hooks. If client retries and hits permissive route, how to attribute? we should attach `validation.outcome` and `fncall_trace_id` to every invocation to correlate.

ridhi: schema for metadata we propose: validation.outcome = one of (accepted, declined, coerced, fallback_accepted); validation.reason short tag; validation.sampled_redacted string if sample allowed; fncall_trace_id string; route_origin route tag.

tom: implementation: put this under a top-level `meta` key to avoid breaking typed SDKs. e.g.: ```json
{
  \"output\": { ... },
  \"meta\": { \"validation.outcome\": \"declined\", \"fncall_trace_id\": \"t_abc123\" }
}
```

ridhI: spelling nit :) but +1 for meta. Also recommend sample storage TTL of 30 days and a PII scrub pipeline with levels: minimal (strip emails), pii (mask tokens), full (store encrypted).

observability-bot: logging note: create counters: validation.declines.by_route, validation.coerced.by_route, validation.sampled_payloads.count. Tag with route and model_variant.

alexa: rollout UX: canary view should show a tiny sparkline of decline%. If decline% > 1% and no opt-in, show a banner and a revert CTA. Add ability to compare strict vs permissive on same time window.

tom: about telemetry sampling: default sample rate 0.5% per route, adjustable by route owners. Add a debug override header 'X-Validation-Debug: true' for internal tests (don't enable for customers).

ridhi: privacy + audit: every sampled payload write must be recorded in an audit log row with who accessed it. Also add a metric for 'sample_view_count' so we can detect overuse.

alexa: action items: 1) tom to open PR adding meta validation fields + fncall_trace_id and telemetry counters 2) ridhi to spec scrub levels + retention + audit rows 3) UX to mock canary compare + redact/button flow (assign to sara) 4) billing to prepare proposal and email finance/legal (billing-bot created thread) 5) observability to add alert rule around spike > 0.5% by route.

sara: (joining) I'll prototype a console mock today. Question: do we want inline expand for redacted snippet or open modal?

tom: start with inline one-line snippet and 'open modal' for the sampled trace (modal requires privileged access).

alexa: thanks all. sync tomorrow 9:30 to review PR and console mock. :thumbsup:
